findings.title: TLS certificate expired or not yet valid
findings.description: The certificate presented by the server is outside its validity window. Browsers show interstitial warnings, training users to click through certificate errors.
findings.remediation: Renew the certificate immediately and automate renewal (e.g. ACME) with expiry monitoring.

findings.title: Deprecated TLS protocol supported
findings.description: The server negotiated or accepted TLS 1.0/1.1 (or older). These protocols are deprecated by RFC 8996 and lack modern cryptographic protections.
findings.evidence: Negotiated: TLSv1.2; legacy handshake accepted: TLSv1.1
findings.remediation: Disable SSLv3, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1. Support TLS 1.2 with AEAD cipher suites and TLS 1.3.

findings.title: HTTPS not available
findings.description: The host serves content over plain HTTP but no working HTTPS endpoint was observed. All traffic, including cookies and credentials, travels in cleartext.
findings.evidence: http://expired.badssl.com/ -> HTTP 200; HTTPS: connection failed: ConnectError
findings.remediation: Provision a valid TLS certificate, serve the application exclusively over HTTPS and redirect all HTTP requests with a 301 to the HTTPS origin.

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy header missing
findings.description: The HTML response does not define a Content-Security-Policy. Without CSP the browser has no policy to restrict script sources, which removes an important mitigation against cross-site scripting and data injection.
findings.evidence: No Content-Security-Policy header or meta tag
findings.remediation: Deploy a restrictive Content-Security-Policy (start with default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self') and tighten it with nonces or hashes. Roll out using Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only first.

findings.title: Server version disclosed in banner
findings.description: The Server header reveals the product and exact version, letting attackers quickly match the host against known vulnerabilities.
findings.remediation: Suppress version details (e.g. nginx 'server_tokens off;', Apache 'ServerTokens Prod' / 'ServerSignature Off').
findings.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options header missing
findings.description: The response does not include 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff'. Browsers may MIME-sniff responses and interpret user-controlled content as script or HTML.
findings.remediation: Send 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' on all responses and ensure accurate Content-Type headers.

findings.title: Clickjacking protection missing (X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors)
findings.description: The HTML response sets neither X-Frame-Options nor a CSP frame-ancestors directive, so the page may be framed by any origin and abused for clickjacking.
findings.remediation: Send 'Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'' (preferred) and/or 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' or 'SAMEORIGIN'.
findings.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

findings.title: Permissions-Policy header missing
findings.description: No Permissions-Policy is defined, so powerful browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation, payment) are not explicitly restricted for this origin and embedded frames.
findings.remediation: Send a Permissions-Policy disabling unused features, e.g. 'Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=()'.

findings.title: Referrer-Policy header missing
findings.description: No Referrer-Policy is defined. Modern browsers default to strict-origin-when-cross-origin, but older clients may leak full URLs (including tokens in query strings) to third parties.

findings.remediation: Deploy a restrictive Content-Security-Policy (start with default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self') and tighten it with nonces or hashes. Roll out using Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only first.

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options header missing
findings.description: The response does not include 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff'. Browsers may MIME-sniff responses and interpret user-controlled content as script or HTML.
findings.remediation: Send 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' on all responses and ensure accurate Content-Type headers.

findings.title: Clickjacking protection missing (X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors)
findings.description: The HTML response sets neither X-Frame-Options nor a CSP frame-ancestors directive, so the page may be framed by any origin and abused for clickjacking.
findings.remediation: Send 'Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'' (preferred) and/or 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' or 'SAMEORIGIN'.
findings.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

findings.title: CORS allows any origin
findings.description: The response is readable cross-origin by any website ('Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *'). This is safe for genuinely public content but must not be applied to responses containing user-specific or internal data.
findings.remediation: Confirm the resource is public. Otherwise replace the wildcard with an explicit origin allowlist.
findings.cwe_name: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

findings.title: Permissions-Policy header missing
findings.description: No Permissions-Policy is defined, so powerful browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation, payment) are not explicitly restricted for this origin and embedded frames.
findings.remediation: Send a Permissions-Policy disabling unused features, e.g. 'Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=()'.

findings.title: Referrer-Policy header missing
findings.description: No Referrer-Policy is defined. Modern browsers default to strict-origin-when-cross-origin, but older clients may leak full URLs (including tokens in query strings) to third parties.
findings.remediation: Send 'Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin' or 'no-referrer' for sensitive applications.
findings.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

findings.title: security.txt not published
findings.description: No RFC 9116 security.txt file was found at /.well-known/security.txt, so researchers have no documented channel to report vulnerabilities.
findings.remediation: Publish /.well-known/security.txt with at least Contact and Expires fields, ideally signed and including a Policy link.
